text: Coccidiosis mainly affects groups of young birds around 3 weeks old: affected birds show lethargy, ruffled feathers, thirst, and diarrhea that may contain blood — without prompt treatment, birds die. Prevention relies mainly on hygiene: keep floors dry, and use proper feeders/drinkers so feed and water aren't soiled by droppings. Preventive medication in drinking water from 2 weeks old: Sulfa 33 (injectable or in water), Amprolium, or Toltrazuril for 3 days; commercial chick starter feed (up to 3 weeks) often already contains Salinomycin, Monensin, or Lasalocid for this purpose. Treatment uses the same medicines but for 5 days instead of 3.
